definition: KDM2B (lysine-demethylase 2B) is a gene on chromosome 12q24 that encodes an epigenetic regulator; heterozygous pathogenic variants in KDM2B (notably including missense variants in the CxxC DNA-binding domain and loss-of-function variants) cause neurodevelopmental disorder with congenital cardiac defects and variable renal and ocular abnormalities (NEDCRO; OMIM #621474), characterized by global developmental delay, intellectual disability, subtle facial dysmorphisms, congenital heart defects, and variable renal, ocular, and systemic anomalies associated with a distinct peripheral blood DNA methylation episignature.

source.title: Delineation of a KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder and its associated DNA methylation signature
source.quote: Lysine-demethylase 2B (KDM2B) encodes an epigenetic regulator and mouse models suggest an important role during development. We set out to determine whether KDM2B variants are associated with NDD.
